title: Lesson 24 first-type causative and destockal review

groups.title: Final vowels and open valence
groups.proposal: Keep the typed verbstem open and never infer its Valence from final i, a, o, or e; let the user choose the intended Valence, then use the vowel patterns and exceptions only as concise reading cues.
groups.writingJob: Accept an open typed stem ending in the attested vowel space, preserve the user's intransitive or transitive Source analysis, and prevent final-vowel tendencies from authorizing or blocking that analysis.
groups.readingJob: Explain the common i/intransitive and a/directive pattern, the many exceptions, nonactive o and hua ambiguity, and a/e variants without turning any example into a stem list.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the stem and chooses its intended Valence. The application reads the final vowel, keeps it visible as a cue, and never uses it to choose Valence.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the open Stem and Source VNC Valence controls; do not add a final-vowel, common-pattern, exception, or Canvas-example control.

groups.title: Valence-neutral Sources and their nonactive results
groups.proposal: Allow the same open stem to be used with an intransitive or transitive Source analysis when the user intends a valence-neutral reading; require the real transitive object and let the chosen member determine its later nonactive route.
groups.writingJob: Represent identical-shape intransitive and transitive Sources without inventing a derivational suffix, require a specific object for the normal transitive use, and pass the selected Valence unchanged into passive or impersonal formation.
groups.readingJob: Explain the usual applicative-like meaning, the rarer causative-like meaning, the a-final and i-final examples, and the distinct nonactive outcomes as lexical and interpretive guidance rather than a whitelist.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses intransitive or transitive Valence and supplies any transitive participant. The application derives object requirements and the later nonactive route; it does not ask whether the stem is on a Canvas list.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source VNC Valence, Object, and later Voice controls; do not add a valence-neutral toggle, applicative-like-versus-causative-like switch, or example picker as grammar authority.

groups.title: Final-i type-one causatives
groups.proposal: After the user chooses Causative for an open intransitive final-i Source, show replacement and addition as the only formation choice that may still be needed: replacement removes i and adds short a, while addition keeps i and adds long ā.
groups.writingJob: Build either the replacive or additive type-one causative from the typed Source, accept an explicitly supplied stem-specific consonant change when required, derive short or long causative a from the boundary, and assign Class B to replacement or Class C to addition.
groups.readingJob: Show the source base, removed or retained i, any supplied consonant change, causative object, resulting class, meaning shifts, and all examples without using the examples as an admission list.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Causative and, when the Source analysis does not already settle it, replacement or addition; a special consonant change is requested only when the intended lexical analysis needs one. The application derives vowel length, target Valence, participant transfer, and verb class.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Derivation and Grammar-supported formation, but populate them from the open typed Source and its declared analysis; do not require selection of a stored stem, and do not add controls for vowel length, class, meaning shift, or example identity.

groups.title: Final-a and root-plus-ya causatives
groups.proposal: For an intransitive final-a Source, use replacement only: replace ordinary final a morphologically even when the spelling stays the same, normally replace root-plus-ya with long ā, and expose a retained-y Source analysis only for a genuine lexical exception.
groups.writingJob: Distinguish ordinary final a from derivational ya in the typed Source, perform the correct replacement, preserve an explicitly supplied retentive-ya exception, and derive the Class B or Class C result from the selected route.
groups.readingJob: Explain invisible morphological replacement, normal ya loss, retained-y exceptions, source and result classes, and the ēhua and yōcoya evidence without treating those examples as the only possible inputs.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Causative; the parsed or supplied Source analysis normally settles ordinary-a versus ya replacement. A retained-y choice appears only when the user intends that exceptional lexical analysis.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the typed Source analysis and Causative formation control; do not add a visible-versus-invisible replacement, long-vowel, class, or Canvas-stem control.

groups.title: Root, stock, and stem structure
groups.proposal: Keep destockal structure as one typed Source analysis: root plus stock formative makes a stock, then stock plus theme makes a verbstem; only the completed verbstem can generate a VNC or feed a causative.
groups.writingJob: Preserve root, stock formative, and theme as ordered source segments, block a bare stock from acting as a stem, and carry the completed intransitive stem into its later causative operation.
groups.readingJob: Show the two derivational steps, ranks, theme terminology, three destockal families, and ya comparisons as clickable structure cues.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies or confirms a destockal Source analysis only when needed. The application derives the root-stock-stem hierarchy and refuses to treat the intermediate stock as a complete VNC Source.
groups.controlPolicy: Use one compact Source-analysis disclosure attached to the open stem; do not add separate rank, step, stock-can-be-stem, theme-name, or destockal-family quiz controls.

groups.title: Ni and hui destockal Sources
groups.proposal: Accept open ni and hui destockal Sources with a long stock vowel, derive the regular harmony cue from the root, preserve a supplied exceptional stock vowel, and apply Class B to the completed intransitive stem.
groups.writingJob: Parse or accept root plus long stock vowel plus ni or hui, check the regular vowel-harmony pattern without using it as a whitelist, preserve explicit exceptional analyses, and project the Source through the Class B finite system.
groups.readingJob: Present the ā, ī, ō, and ē inventories, productivity notes, long-root-vowel cautions, meanings, and perfective examples as searchable guidance rather than selectable grammar authority.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the full stem or confirms its segmentation; only an exceptional stock-vowel analysis may require a choice. The application derives the regular harmony cue and Class B behavior.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the open Stem and compact Source-analysis disclosure; do not add an inventory picker, productivity, harmony, stock-vowel, theme, or class control when the typed segmentation already determines it.

groups.title: Ni and hui causative formation
groups.proposal: After the user chooses Causative, ask for replacement versus addition only when the ni or hui Source analysis has not already settled it; then derive Class B for replacement and Class C for addition.
groups.writingJob: Apply either final-i replacement or full-stem addition to an open typed ni or hui destockal Source, preserve that selected history, and derive the correct causative vowel and finite class.
groups.readingJob: Show the majority preferences and listed exceptions for ni and hui as guidance, together with the example meanings and perfectives, without limiting either procedure to a stored list.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Causative and, only where still unresolved, replacement or addition. The application derives target structure, vowel length, participant transfer, and Class B or C.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Grammar-supported formation as a short two-option choice when both analyses remain possible; do not add majority, rare, listed-stem, causative-vowel, or class controls.

groups.title: Coalesced and obsolete destockal Sources
groups.proposal: Preserve a user-supplied underlying root-stock boundary even when identical vowels coalesce in writing, and permit a reconstructed or obsolete Source to feed a later derivation without pretending it is an ordinary attested finite stem.
groups.writingJob: Keep the underlying root and identical stock vowel separate in the formula, coalesce them only in the written projection, and retain typed reconstructed or obsolete source status through later causative formation.
groups.readingJob: Explain the mīni, xīni, cēhui, pōni, and tōni reconstructions, asterisk notation, meanings, and later derivational use as evidence and clickable analysis.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies or confirms the underlying segmented analysis when the surface is coalesced and may identify a reconstructed Source when that history is intended. The application performs coalescence and preserves provenance automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Use the compact Source-analysis disclosure only when the surface hides a boundary; do not add coalesce, double-vowel, asterisk, obsolete-stem, or example controls.

groups.title: Hua destockal Sources and replacement causatives
groups.proposal: Accept open ā-hua and ē-hua destockal analyses, keep independently entered hua and hui synonyms separate, and form the type-one causative only by morphological hua to hu-a replacement, even when the visible stem spelling is unchanged.
groups.writingJob: Preserve typed stock and hua structure, perform licensed coalescence, carry the Source's Class A or supplied A/B analysis, distinguish destockal from compound structure when needed, reconstruct a missing intransitive mate when explicitly analyzed, and derive a Class B replacement causative.
groups.readingJob: Show lexical meanings, nounroot resemblance readings, independent synonym pairs, class variation, dictionary gaps, and examples without a stem whitelist or a synonym-conversion control.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the open Source and confirms a destockal, compound, exceptional class, or reconstructed-source analysis only when ambiguity requires it. Causative replacement and the Class B target are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the compact Source-analysis and Causative controls; do not add hua-versus-hui synonym, resemblance meaning, dictionary listing, visible replacement, or target-class controls.

groups.title: Short-vowel hui Sources and o-ā causatives
groups.proposal: For an open i-hui or a-hui destockal Source, derive the short stock vowel from the root when regular, replace the whole i-hui or a-hui ending with o-ā for the causative, handle o-hui coalescence, and preserve exact negative or irregular relations without turning the examples into an admission list.
groups.writingJob: Build and validate short-vowel hui structure, apply the root-vowel and root-final-l conditions, derive the o-ā Class C causative from a Class B Source, and block or admit an exceptional relation only through a real typed lexical restriction or irregular source analysis.
groups.readingJob: Show the opposite harmony pattern, long-vowel hui contrast, o-hui note, lexical gaps, pilihui and pilca distinction, meanings, and examples as detailed guidance.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies or confirms exceptional source structure only when the regular root-conditioned analysis cannot decide it. The application derives regular stock choice, causative replacement, classes, and any exact negative restriction.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the compact Source-analysis and Causative controls; do not add stock-vowel, replace-ending, class, note, gap, or Canvas-example controls, and do not gate open valid stems through an inventory.

groups.title: Causative subject and object transfer
groups.proposal: Keep Imported subject as the real user choice: the application turns an active intransitive Source subject into a specific projective or reflexive causative object, or an impersonal intransitive Source subject into nonspecific tla, then builds the new causative subject around it.
groups.writingJob: Consume the complete typed active or impersonal intransitive Source, objectivize its subject with the correct specific, reflexive, or nonspecific carrier, import the selected causer as the new subject, and preserve the Source core inside the causative result.
groups.readingJob: Trace the tomi, nitomi, and tomōhua transformations line by line, show source subject to object transfer, explain reflexive responsibility and translation overlap, and keep every example subordinate to the canonical participant transform.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the imported causative subject and supplies the Source; projective versus reflexive is chosen only when the active Source subject and new subject make that a real coreference choice. The application derives the object kind from Source voice and participant identity.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Imported subject and a conditional participant-coreference choice; do not ask the user to choose source-subject objectivization, specific versus nonspecific carrier, tla, formula line, tense carried from context, or translation wording.
